placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an observatory instrument calibration report — instrument identity, calibration value, and verification method — and no existing strata category (none yet exist in this repo) covers organizational record-keeping around instrument calibration. This is a foundational organizational category, not itself a theme, so it needs no parent.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as an organizational record category
placements.frame: Does this content report an instrument's calibration status, verification method, or standard against which correctness is judged?

placements.title: Correctness is arbitrated by external reference standards, not self-report
placements.frame: Does this calibration claim ground its validity in verification against a fixed external reference (plates, standards), or does it rest on the instrument's or speaker's own asserted status?
placements.why: All three expressions assert the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration status but consistently ground that assertion's correctness in verification against the June reference plates rather than in bare say-so — src-1 states this discursively ('We verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds'), while src-2 and src-3 restate the same grounding in terse field-label form ('verified against June reference plates'). This is a recurring validation-practice theme future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (new instruments, new reference sets), not a one-time fact — the specific value 88.4 MHz is the fact this leaf's theme evidences, not the leaf itself.
